acceptance_condition: A proved lower bound N(H) >= g(H) with explicit constants, including exact analysis of the chain recurrence and, for any subtree argument, proved lower bounds on distinct children per vertex and proved upper bounds on per-level height growth; if only a logarithmic bound is provable, a precise statement of what blocks the power bound.
rationale: D5 is an independent obligation from D4; lower bounds require constructive family arguments of a different character than tree-counting upper bounds, so it runs as its own thread.
text: From first principles, prove the strongest rigorous lower bound attainable for N(H). Construct explicit infinite families of solutions with controlled height growth and prove their members are distinct: at minimum a single chain (e.g., (1,1,1,3) -> (1,1,3,11) -> (1,1,11,41) -> ... generated by repeatedly mutating the second-largest coordinate) giving N(H) >= c log H with an explicit constant from the chain's growth rate (analyze the associated linear recurrence exactly); then attack a power lower bound N(H) >= c H^alpha by exhibiting a subtree in which every vertex has at least 2 (or more) provably distinct children whose maxima grow by a bounded factor per level, and determine the best provable alpha. If a power bound cannot be proved, identify the precise obstruction (e.g., inability to control the growth factor along branching edges, or collisions between children). All families must be proved to consist of solutions (direct substitution into a^2+b^2+c^2+d^2 = 4abcd) and proved distinct.
